name: 3.1 Terminology
_note: PUSHED 2026-08-10. Fills the gap left when 3.3 went first — 3.1 and 3.2 did not exist on disk then. All eleven questions come from the existing bank and none has ever been filed (checked against reference/question-library.json), so this push is 11 new library questions plus 11 attaches. Sub-topic coverage follows OpenStax 3.1: sample space (1,2), probability of a single event (3,4,5,6), events as sets and the probability of set operations (7,8,9), and conditional notation ahead of the 3.3 formula (10,11). Ramp is 3 easy / 6 medium / 2 hard, close to the 30/50/20 in assessment-presets. Points total exactly 100: five 6s, one 10, five 12s. Undated like everything else in the master.

questions.title: Count Outcomes - sample space sizes for coins, for dice, and for a mixed coin-and-die experiment
Urn Draw - the size of the sample space, the probability of one colour, and the complement of that colour
Probability of a Named Card Category - a single draw from a 52-card deck
Probability of Exactly One Head - exactly one head across n coin flips, where the trap is counting orderings
Probability the Two-Dice Sum Equals a Target - count the favourable ordered pairs out of the 36
Three Children Genders - P(exactly two of one gender) and P(at least one), on the eight-outcome sample space
Set Operations on Dice Events - write A union B, A intersect B and A complement as sets of outcomes, before any probability is taken
Probability of Set Operations on Dice Events - P(A union B), P(A intersect B) and P(A complement) for two events on one die
Probability of King or Heart - an OR across two overlapping card categories, counted from the deck rather than from the addition formula
Identify the Conditioning Event - pick the conditioning event out of a worded conditional probability statement
Conditional Probability via the Reduced Sample Space - given the sum of two dice, find the size of the reduced space and two conditional probabilities on it
Pre-FRQ Grade a Probability Setup - A two-dice probability scenario with a grading checklist, where the student grades four sample responses against the rubric instead of writing one
